general.title: Lesson Test
general.description: This virtual learning object "Lesson Test" that makes part of the lesson No: 2, At the Comic Book Store, which in turn belongs to the Starter (A1.2) of the teaching of English as a Foreign Language, is intended to work on: make and respond to offers and invitations; say what you want to do, would prefer to do; ask and say what people are doing at the moment; make and respond to requests;make and respond to suggestions; say what you like or dislike. The grammar of this LO refers to: simple present in affirmative, negative and interrogative forms; modal verbs for requests, suggestions and invitations; simple present in affirmative, and interrogative forms; present continuous in affirmative, and interrogative forms; verbs with infinitives: have to, need to, (would) like to, want to; imperative: let's; Wh/Hw questions. Also, the vocabulary considers: hobbies, interests, sports; jobs and work; times of the day; days of the week;travel and transportation. Finally, the pronunciation in this LO is consonant-vowel linking; minimal pairs and consonant clusters, e.g. /ʧ/ and /ʃ/ sounds.

description.recommendedUse: This digital resource can be used as an activity that allows the learner to reflect on the use of grammar of English language in different communicative contexts. The instructor can work further on activities and tasks that help learners to improve their procedural knowledge.

description.learningGoal: The purpose of this learning object is to accurately use information, involving apologies, thanks, suggestions and invitations in communicative situations; accurately explain information about interests, hobbies, and preferences in communicative situations.

resource.description: This lesson: "At the Comic Book Store" belongs to Starter (A1.2). It is composed of twelve learning objects, that have the following learning outcomes: accurately use information, involving apologies, thanks, suggestions and invitations in communicative situations; accurately explain information about interests, hobbies, and preferences in communicative situations. On the other hand, the communicative functions of this lesson are: make and respond to offers and invitations; say what you want to do, would prefer to do; ask and say what people are doing at the moment; make and respond to requests; make and respond to suggestions; say what you like or dislike.
